senses.gloss: (b. h.) to go, go away; to walk.
units: <cite ref="Yevamot 84a:3">Yeb. 84ᵃ</cite> <he>כשהָלַכְתִּי וכ׳</he> when I left home to study with &c.

<cite ref="Makkot 10b:2">Macc. 10ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>בדרך שאדם רוצה לֵילֵךְ בה מוֹלִיכִין אותו</he> whatever way one desires to go, one is led; a. v. fr.—<he>הוֹלְכֵי מדברות</he> travellers through the desert.
Y. Kidd. I, 61ᵈ כהולכים בתורת ד׳ (not בה׳) as though they did walk in the law &c.—Imper. לֵךְ, לְכָה, v. כָּלָה Pi., a. כַּלֵּךְ.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 9:2">Ḥull. IX, 2</cite> (<cite ref="Chullin 122a">122ᵃ</cite>) <he>או שהי׳ בהן</he> (Mish. ed. <he>שהלך</he>) or trod upon them for tanning purposes.
<cite ref="Eruvin 100b:7">Erub. 100ᵇ</cite> <he>שיְהַלֵּךְ ע״ג וכ׳</he> to tread upon plants.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 39:8">Gen. R. s. 39</cite> <he>מְהַלֵּךְ בארם וכ׳</he> travelling through Aram &c.—
<cite ref="Ketubot 60a">Keth. 60ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Keritot 22a:4">Ker. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>מְהַלְּכֵי שתים</he> walking on two legs (human beings); a. fr.

senses.gloss: to cause opening of the bowels. Y. Kil. I, 27ᵃ top מְהַלֶּכֶת את בני מיעים; cmp. הִילּוּךְ. [Y. Keth. XII, 35ᵇ top מהלך לפניהן אל הארץ, v. חָלַד.]

units: <cite ref="Gittin 4a:13">Gitt. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>המוֹלִיךְ וכ׳</he> he who carries abroad a letter of divorce, contrad. to <he>המביא</he> he who brings a letter from abroad.
<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 3:9">Ab. Zar. III, 9</cite> <he>יוֹלִיךְ הנאה וכ׳</he> let him cast the profit (one loaf’s value) into the Sea.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 6:1">Gitt. VI, 1</cite> <he>הוֹלֵךְ גט וכ׳</he> carry this letter of divorce (as a messenger).

<cite ref="Gittin 63a:1">Ib. 63ᵃ</cite> sq. (distinction between <he>הילך</he>, here is the letter of divorce, i.e. take possession of it in behalf of my wife, and <he>הולך</he> carry it, i.e. be my messenger).
<cite ref="Gittin 64a">Ib. 64ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>הולך כזכי דמי</he> ‘carry’ (the letter of divorce) is equal to ‘take possession’ (in behalf of her who authorized thee); a. fr.
Cant. R. to V, 1; Gen. R. s. 19 (ref. to Gen. III, 8) מְהַלֵּךְ … אלא מִתְהַלֵּךְ וכ׳ it does not say m’hallekh (walking) but mith-hallekh, He hastened and went upward.
<cite ref="Genesis 3:8">Ib.</cite> <he>מתהלך לו</he> (ed. <he>מת הלך</he>, corr. acc., v. Matt. K.) is he (Adam) going away (from God)?, v. <cite ref="A03423"><he>אתמהא</he></cite>.
